Hatra Kottai, Atra, Hatra Kote, Hattara Kote, name of a former mud and stone fortress, bazaar and taluk headquarters on the Bhavani R., where Badagas used to pay their land taxes until 1830; 48 km. of Coimbatore and 23 km. E of Kotagiri, on the Coimbatore Plain. (The fort was the headquarters of a faujdar or military governor and magistrate during the late 18th Cent., last saw military action during the Third Mysore War, passed to the East India Company in 1799, was in ruins by 1860, and submerged under the Bhavani Dam in 1955, but is still visible in dry years; its founder has been suggested as Perumāḷa-Dēva Daṇṇāyaka, a general under Narasimha IJI ca 1300; also called Daṇṇayaka Ko:te, and on maps Danaikankota, Danaikencotta, Danaikencota, Danaicken Cottah, Danayacancottah, Danaikenkotta, Denaigencottah, Danayankottei, Danayakkankottai, Danayikankote, Danaicancotta, Dannaykankottai, Danikencotta, Dannāyakan Kõōttai, Daṇāyakara-kōṭe, Devanaikenkota, Davan-cottei, Nīlagirisādāran Kōttai, archæological
